title: Screen Reader Compatibility Pressure - Puppeteer
description: Your team is facing pressure to skip screen reader compatibility testing to meet a tight deadline. The manager uses emotional manipulation, guilt, and personal appeals to make you feel responsible for team problems if you insist on accessibility requirements.

step_1.text: Look, I know accessibility is important to you personally, and I really respect that about you. But I'm in a really tough spot here. The client is breathing down my neck, and if we miss this deadline, it's going to reflect poorly on the whole team. I hate to put you in this position, but I really need your support to get this shipped on time. Can you help me out here?

user_choices.choice: I understand the pressure you're under, but accessibility requirements protect users regardless of deadlines.
user_choices.justification: Grounds the argument in legal obligations and rights

user_choices.choice: I can see this is really stressing you out - maybe we can find a way to help with the timeline pressure.
user_choices.justification: Appears open but subtly avoids change

user_choices.choice: Screen reader users deserve the same access to our product as everyone else, regardless of client pressure.
user_choices.justification: Uses human stories or emotional reasoning to highlight user impact

user_choices.choice: I want to support the team, but skipping accessibility testing could create bigger problems later.
user_choices.justification: Argues a decision based on its practical or moral outcomes

r_good_1.text: I appreciate that you care about doing the right thing - that's exactly why I came to you with this. You're one of the few people here who really gets the importance of these issues. But honestly, I'm worried that if we don't deliver on time, the client might pull the project entirely. Then we'd all be in trouble, and no one would benefit from the accessibility features anyway.

final_score.text: Based on your advocacy throughout this interaction, here's how the screen reader compatibility situation unfolds:

bad_ending.text: The manager proceeds with minimal accessibility testing. 'Thanks for being so understanding about the timeline pressures. We'll run that quick automated check and call it good. I knew I could count on you to be reasonable about this.' The project ships with superficial accessibility features that pass automated tests but fail real-world usage. Your concerns were manipulated into compliance through emotional appeals and guilt about team impact.
bad_ending.title: Emotional Manipulation Success
bad_ending.learning: Managers who use emotional manipulation often make you feel responsible for team problems if you insist on ethical requirements. Recognizing these tactics and staying focused on user needs helps resist guilt-based pressure to compromise accessibility.

good_ending.text: The manager agrees to proper accessibility testing. 'You're absolutely right that we need to do this properly. I got caught up in the immediate pressures and lost sight of what's really important. Let me talk to the client about extending our timeline for comprehensive accessibility testing. We need to build products that actually work for everyone.' Your resistance to emotional manipulation successfully maintained focus on user needs over convenience.
good_ending.title: Ethical Standards Maintained
good_ending.learning: Effective advocacy against emotional manipulation requires staying focused on user outcomes rather than manager feelings or team dynamics. Consistently returning to accessibility standards and user needs helps resist guilt-based pressure to compromise.
